signals: DROP or RENAME; NOT NULL without a default; type change; index built without a concurrent option; backfill in the deploy; code and schema changed in one step instead of expand then contract; missing down migration
worst: S3 downtime from locks; S4 data loss; a revert does not undo it

signals: removed or renamed endpoint, field, argument or route; new required input; narrowed type or enum; changed status code or error shape; wire field renumbered; new enum or union member that exhaustive clients reject
worst: S3 for every client still on the old shape, including installed apps that cannot update

signals: changed middleware, policy, role or ownership checks; session, token or cookie flags; CORS or CSP; tenant filters; secrets handling
worst: S4 exposure when checks loosen; S3 lockout when they tighten

signals: major version bumps; runtime (not dev) lockfile churn; framework, language runtime or base image upgrade
worst: Wide and hard to trace; read the changelog for breaking changes

signals: changed defaults; renamed environment variables; a flag default flipped on; timeouts, pool sizes, rate limits
worst: Wide; config skips the tests code gets

signals: changed build, deploy or pipeline steps; base image, resource limits, routing or scaling rules; a job removed from the required set
worst: Wide S3 when a deploy or rollback path breaks; often invisible until the next release

signals: edits to global, reset or element selectors, forced style overrides, design tokens, theme variables, stacking order, position or overflow on layout primitives; changed props, defaults or markup of a component with many importers
worst: Wide S1 to S3: layout breaks or controls hidden on screens the author never opened

signals: changed conditionals around rendering, removed handlers, changed routes or links, text expansion, removed loading or error states
worst: Narrow to Feature, S2 to S3

signals: hard-coded strings; removed or renamed translation keys; string concatenation; locale-blind date, number or currency formatting
worst: S1 to S2 for non-default locales

signals: removed or skipped tests, loosened assertions, deleted fixtures for behavior the diff still changes
worst: No user effect alone; lowers confidence in every other finding

signals: user-facing instructions that no longer match the merged behavior
worst: S1 unless the doc is the product (API reference, runbook)

signals: removed labels, alternative text or accessibility roles; a generic container replacing a button or link; removed focus outline or keyboard handlers; focus traps; lowered contrast
worst: S3 for keyboard and screen reader users, even when few

signals: delete or update without a scope or tenant filter; changed idempotency, retries, rounding, precision, timezone or encoding; removed validation
worst: S4 corrupted or wrong data, often silent

signals: changed cache keys, lifetimes or invalidation; changed shape of stored, cached, queued, cookie or local storage payloads
worst: Old and new versions cannot read each other during rollout or after a revert

signals: query in a loop or render path; query without a limit; removed index, batching or memoization; synchronous network call on a hot path; larger bundle or binary
worst: S2, S3 when it times out
